_comment: The patcher window's "?" guides. One short, plain guide for every public patch (by patch id), every population mode (by mode id) and every button, tool and setting (by control key). Each guide is a list of short lines: what it does, how to use it, and what to watch out for. tests/test_how_to_use.py refuses a public patch, mode or control without one, and a guide that is too long or uses technical words. Write each from what the feature really does (its description in the patcher, README and How to Use.txt).

guide: Lets the game play in another language. Choose the language in Tools, Translations...; the game uses it from its next start, no re-patching.
On by default, and English until you choose a language: then the game is exactly as without this patch.
Lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Words painted into pictures stay English.
Letters the game's font lacks (Turkish, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese) need Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts too.

deselect_all.title: Deselect All Patches
guide: Unticks every patch, so you can tick just the ones you want.

unicode_font.title: Unicode Font
guide: The typeface Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts) draws all of the game's text in: pick one of the fonts Windows has, or leave Segoe UI.
It is written next to the game as VVFP Unicode Font.txt the next time you patch with Use Unicode Font ticked; patch again after changing it.
Characters the typeface lacks come from Windows' other fonts, then the bundled open fonts (Noto, Unifont, Last Resort).
It does nothing while Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts is used instead.
The box is in the Settings... window beside each game's Use Unicode Font row; one typeface is shared by every game.

meal_multiplier.title: Hungrier Villagers

The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).
A number saved above 10 is 10. A number like 0.3 takes that much on average (a meal is whole food).
Drag the slider or type the number in the box beside it (then press Enter).

island_frequency_multiplier.title: More Frequent Island Events

The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).

louder_flutes_multiplier.title: Louder Wind Flutes

The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).
The loudest moments are held just under the loudest a sound can be, so the flutes never distort; higher numbers make the quiet parts louder.
At 5, with the game's Sound and Music at their maximum, the flutes are heard over the music.
It is written into the game the next time you patch with Louder Wind Flutes ticked; patch again after changing it. Owner's Defaults sets it to 5.
It does nothing while Louder Wind Flutes is not ticked.

sickness_multiplier.title: 0.1-10x Sickness

village_solidarity_strength.title: Village Solidarity strength

At 1x each point away from 50 adds 2% to a favoured event's or ending's own chance (double at 0 or 100); at 2x 4% a point, at 0.5x 1%.

tech_cost_multiplier.title: 0.1-10x Tech Cost

patch_selection_settings.title: Patch Selection Settings

patch_search.title: Search patch names
guide: Type part of a patch's name to show only the patches in this game whose names match.
Only names are searched, not descriptions. Clear the box to show every patch again.
Searching never ticks or unticks anything.

output_location.title: Modded output location
guide: Click Choose Folder... to pick where the modded copies go.
Each game is made inside it as "(Game name) - Modded".
Leave it blank to put each copy beside its original game folder.
A deep folder is fine. The games can only open files whose full path is 259 characters or less, so if one of the game's own files would be deeper, nothing is written:
the patcher names that file and says how many characters shorter the folder must be. A folder near the top of a drive, such as C:\Games, always works.

choose_exe.title: Original game executable
guide: Click Browse... and choose the original game's .exe, as downloaded from Last Day of Work.
The blue line below says which game it found.
The original game is never changed.

validate.title: Validate
guide: Checks that the chosen game is a supported original, and shows the population limit of the mode you picked.
Nothing is written.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
guide: A practice run: checks the game and prepares every ticked patch, but writes no files.
Shows where the modded copy would be made.

create_modified_exe.title: Create Modified EXE
guide: 1. Pick a population mode and tick the patches you want.
2. Browse to the original game's .exe, then click Create Modified EXE.
A complete copy named "(Game name) - Modded" is made with the modded game in it; the original is never changed.
The patcher's own files go in a "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files" folder inside the copy.
Play the .exe in the copy. Its saves go in their own "- Modded" folder in Documents\LDW.
Patching again replaces the copy (it asks first); your saves are not touched.

game_folders.title: Game folders
guide: Choose one folder per game, each holding that game's original .exe.
Use Choose Folder... on a row, or Find All 5 in Parent Folder... to fill them all.
The original folders are never changed.

find_all_5.title: Find All 5 in Parent Folder
guide: Choose one folder that holds your five games.
The patcher finds each game's .exe in that folder or one folder below, and fills in the rows.

validate_all_5.title: Validate All 5
guide: Checks that all five chosen games are supported originals.
Nothing is written.

dry_run_all_5.title: Dry Run All 5
guide: A practice run for all five games: checks them and prepares every ticked patch, but writes no files.

patch_all_5.title: Patch All 5
guide: 1. Pick a population mode and tick the patches you want.
2. Fill in all five game folders, then click Patch All 5.
Each game gets a complete copy named "(Game name) - Modded"; the originals are never changed.
The patcher's own files go in a "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files" folder inside each copy.
Copying five games can take several minutes.

open_vanilla_folder.title: Open Vanilla Folder
guide: Opens the original game's folder in File Explorer.

open_modified_folder.title: Open Modified Folder
guide: Opens the modded copy's folder in File Explorer, where the modded game's .exe is.
Patch the game first.

open_game_folder.title: Open Game Folder
guide: After patching, opens the new modded folder in File Explorer.

back_up_saves.title: Back Up Saves
guide: Copies a game's save folders (your saves and the patcher's logs) into a dated Backups folder inside each one.
Click Back Up Saves, tick the save folders you want, then Back Up Selected.
The game can stay open: it is paused for the copy, but the backup holds the village as of its last save.
Old backups are never replaced or deleted.
Back up before Start Over: Start Over wipes everything the Fun Patcher kept for that save: all its logs (the Village History too),
all its data (the Elder Totems too) and its family tree files. It keeps Backups, Copies Made Before Repairs and tree pictures.
Every save in the backup is set to Paused, always. Other saves are not touched.

restore_saves.title: Restore Saves
guide: Puts a backup back: the whole save folder, or one save slot.
Quit the game first, from its own menu.
Choose a backup, choose whole folder or one slot, then Restore...; you are shown what will change first.
Your saves as they are now are backed up first, so a restore can be undone.
Delete Backup... removes a backup you no longer want (it asks first).
Details... shows the chosen backup's tribes: population, food, tech points, last saved and last played.

backups.title: Backups
guide: Shows every backup of one save folder, newest first, with its date and time, size and the save slots it holds.
Choose a backup to see each tribe in it: population, food, tech points, technology levels, speed and difficulty.
Last saved is the save file's own time; last played is the save's own last moment, when the game last ran.
Population counts living villagers and babies on the way; in New Believers only believers (Heathens apart).
A value that cannot be read says unknown. It only reads: nothing is changed.
Restore Saves has Details... for the chosen backup, and Repair Saves & Logs a Backups... button.

rename_tribe.title: Rename Tribe
guide: Changes a tribe's name inside its save.
Quit the game first, from its own menu.
Pick the game, save folder and tribe, type the new name and click Rename.
The save folder is backed up first, so you can undo it with Restore Saves.
The patcher's logs carry on for the same village under the new name.

copy_player_slot.title: Copy Player Slot
guide: Copies a village into another save slot of the same game, under a new name. Quit the game first.
A slot with no save file is empty, whatever the slot list says; a slot with a player is overwritten. You are asked first; No (also Return or Escape) changes nothing.
The folder is backed up first, as (before copy). The slot's old files go to Backups, Replaced by copy, never deleted; Restore Saves brings them back.
The copy takes its logs, data and trees along, its record numbers after the game's highest.
Not copied: a repair waiting to run, and the family tree reports and Matchmaker text (made again any time).
Choose Move to move the village itself, keeping its name: its save, the game's older copies, logs, data, trees and repair copies all go along; its old slot is left empty.
Move lists every file it will move before you say Yes, backs the folder up first, as (before move), and keeps the target slot's old files in Backups, Replaced by move.
Choose Delete to send every file of a slot to the Recycle Bin: its save, logs, data, trees, repair copies and its files in every backup. Pictures stay.
Delete lists every file and asks twice; No changes nothing. No backup is made: put anything back from the Recycle Bin.

check_logs.title: Check Saves & Logs
guide: Checks whether the patcher's logs and data files for a village agree with its save.
That includes masks still kept for villagers who are no longer in the village.
Pick the game, save folder and tribe, then click Check.
Each file is marked OK, WRONG, NOTE or UNCHECKED.
It also says what older records lack (Sex, titles, masks, Twin / Triplet) that Repair Saves & Logs can add.
It only reads, so the game may stay open.

repair_logs.title: Repair Saves & Logs
guide: Quit the game first, then pick the game, save folder and tribe; the logs are checked.
Tick what to do, then Repair (backed up first). Reset corrupted skill values, old "?" names, children's "Apprentice" Job lines.
New Believers: Catch up Heathen ages adds the time each villager spent among the Heathens to their age (the list is shown first).
Older records get the Sex, Special villager, Custom title, Mask and Twin / Triplet lines they lack; you are asked what files cannot tell.
Give villagers last names (Choose...): village rule, own rule or Random; in the game and every log.
Number duplicate names: Soda I, Soda II..., oldest first (order of appearance), in game and logs.
Fix grave information (Choose...): where a grave and its records differ, pick the value, or edit a grave.
Let the game repair: play the tribe, quit from its menu (needs a patch that keeps logs). Move Old Files to New Names / Move Files to Save Folders: repatch first.
Game speed: in the save, or in a backup (Set the speed in a backup...); always works.

family_tree_maker.title: Family Tree Maker
guide: Draws a village's family tree from its save and the patcher's logs: who descends from whom, and each villager's generation.
Pick the game, save folder and tribe. Give the game's folder too, so each villager shows their own head.
Click a villager to select them; Ctrl+click adds one, Shift+click a run, Ctrl+A everyone, Shift+drag a box.
Drag anything to move it; smart guides, snap to grid and Align line things up. Drag empty space to move around; the mouse wheel or + and - zoom.
Right-click anything to change its colour. Retype any portrait, give special villagers a marked border, choose fonts and backgrounds.
Add pictures, the games' logos and text boxes; drag, resize, turn and flip them. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Z and the other Windows shortcuts work.
Help (F1) lists every control. Ctrl+S saves an editable tree; Export as Picture: PNG or JPG. Only Number duplicate names edits the save (it asks).

village_matchmaker.title: Village Matchmaker
guide: Suggests which villagers to pair, by rules you choose. Every rule is a tick box you can switch on or off.
Rules include no shared ancestors, how closely related a pair may be, each kind of close family, closeness in age and different last names.
Ages are 18 to 49 unless you tick Allow 50 and older, or Plan ahead to include everyone.
It suggests only: nothing in the game is changed. The suggestions are also saved beside the tribe's logs.
Your ticks are remembered for next time.

game_mechanics.title: Game Mechanics
guide: For the curious: shows the hidden rules of one village, worked out from its save.
Choose a game, its save folder and a tribe. The page groups what it finds: food sources, refills, the farmers needed to feed the village (live and while catching up) and more.
Every time is a real date and time, at the save's game speed. For The Secret City: each fruit tree, when it was planted, when it refills and when it can be picked.
It counts the techs the village has and the patches in the game that change a rule, when it can find that game's folder.
It only reads: nothing is changed, so the game may be running (it shows the save as it was last written).

stew_recipes.title: Stew Recipes
guide: Every stew the cauldron makes in The Lost Children, The Secret City and The Tree of Life, one tab each.
Each recipe lists its herbs by the names the game shows, the water it takes, and what happens when a villager eats it.
The Lost Children's plants have no names in the game, so the patcher names them by colour.
It also says which stews solve puzzles and what else they need, how much food a stew takes, and whether a stew can kill.
It reads nothing from your saves and changes nothing. A line in red marked UNCONFIRMED is one the game's code does not settle.

custom_island_event_library.title: Custom Island Event Library
guide: Write your own island events with questions, choices and random outcomes, then pick one to happen from Custom Island Events in the game.
Any part can be a question with two to four buttons, as often as you like; each answer shows a page of its own first.
An award can be a range, and differ per game. An event can need puzzles solved first, roles at most so many years apart, and check the game's patches.
Each event is kept in the save folder of the game chosen at the top; the game lists only the events that pass every check.
The tree on the left shows every part by its name (Rename on the Text tab); the tabs on the right edit the chosen part: its text, its ways on and weights, its changes.
The Check tab lists every problem (click one to go to it) and the chances of every outcome. The fit meter shows the text fits, scrolling if the game has Scrolling Popups.
If no villager fits a role the event needs, the game refuses to queue the event. (Name) is the full name when Last Names is on.
Delete moves an event to the Recycle Bin. Export and Import share an event as a file. The two New from buttons start from the shipped examples.

picture_studio.title: Picture Studio
guide: Draws villagers exactly as each game draws them and saves them as clear-background PNG pictures, in all five games.
From my save: pick the game, save folder and save, then anyone in it. Pick the pose, direction and frame under the picture.
Make your own: any head, body, mask, sex, age, life stage, pose and frame the game has, plus the patcher's own masks, grey hair and head look.
Everything: every picture the game has, drawn the game's way and sorted by kind (animals, buildings, the Tech screen, meters, buttons, screens). Unused art is marked (unused).
Save at the game's size, 2x, 4x or your own size; save one picture, a group or the whole village into a folder.
The pictures come from your own game folder (click Find game... the first time if asked). Saves are only read, never changed.

unicode_font_tool.title: Unicode Font
guide: Chooses the typeface Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts) draws all of a game's text with. The default is Segoe UI.
Pick any font installed in Windows (type in the search box to narrow the list) or choose a .ttf, .otf or .ttc font file.
The preview draws both of the game's fonts as the game will, fitted so a line is as wide as the game's own. A character the font lacks comes from the fallback fonts.
Save remembers the choice; patch the game again to use it. A font file is copied into the game's patcher folder and loaded for the game only, never installed in Windows.
The Unicode Font box beside the setting, and --unicode-font on the command line, write the same choice.

game_text.title: Game Text
guide: Opens Picture Studio's Text tab: type anything and see it drawn in a game's own fonts, in colour or see-through, and save it as a PNG.
Pick the font, size, colour and zoom. Tick "As the stock game shows it" to see the unpatched game, or "As Use Unicode Font draws it" to see the typeface you chose in Unicode Font.
Insert character... searches by name or code point and labels each character (game), (patcher-made), (drawn by Windows: the font) or (missing).
Nothing in a game or a save is changed.

translations.title: Translations
guide: Pick the game, then a Language: the patched game uses it from its next start. English (original) is the game's own words.
Needs the Translations row (on by default). Make a translation: the editor lists every English line, patches' text too.
Add translation file... (or drop one here) checks and adds a file. Download from GitHub... gets shared ones.
Ctrl+click, Shift+click, Ctrl+A or Select All pick several files. Export... copies them (several into one folder).
Delete... moves them to the Recycle Bin after one Yes/No (No is the default). English can't be deleted; a deleted language in use goes back to English.
Share on GitHub...: answer Yes, type a credit name, then drag the file into the page that opens.
Email addresses are never saved and are rejected from translation files.

check_logs_automatically.title: Check logs automatically
guide: On by default. Games you create while it is ticked check each village's logs quietly while you play.
Only if something is wrong, you are asked Repair or Not now when you close the game, never during play.
Repair fixes it (backed up first); Not now changes nothing and asks again next time.
To turn it off, untick this box and patch the game again; a game already made keeps its own setting.

check_for_updates.title: Check for updates
guide: Opens the patcher's GitHub page, where the newest version is listed.
Your version is shown just above the link.

collectible_frequency_multiplier.title: Collectible and Mushroom Frequency
guide: How many times as often mushrooms and collectibles appear on their own with the Collectible and Mushroom Frequency patch: 0.1 to 10 in steps of 0.1, 1 unless you move it.
The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).
It is written into each game the next time you patch with Collectible and Mushroom Frequency ticked; patch again after changing it.
Owner's Defaults sets it to 1. It does nothing while the patch is not ticked.

food_gain_multiplier.title: Food Gained per Food Source
guide: How many times its normal food each food source gives with the Food Gained per Food Source patch: 0.1 to 10 in steps of 0.1, 1 unless you move it.
The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).

The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).

The slider reads -10 (a tenth) to 10 (10 times); 1, the middle, is the normal game, and -2 is half. Drag it or type the number in the box (then press Enter).

difficulty_sliders.title: Difficulty Sliders
guide: Opens the page with every slider: Tech Cost, Hungrier Villagers, Sickness, More Frequent Island Events, Louder Wind Flutes, Village Solidarity and the five newer ones.
They are grouped by game, with each patch's name beside its slider. A slider is used only while its patch is ticked on the main page.
Each reads -10 to 10: 10 is 10 times, -10 a tenth, -2 half, and 1, the middle, the normal game. A number saved above 10 is 10.
One number is shared by every game that has the patch. Patch again after changing a slider.
